title: A college dance, a fraternity party and Max reciting the Gettysburg Address
summary: After the dance Barefield urged leaving the fraternity house before the troopers arrived. At a Howard Johnson's that would not serve them, Max stood on a stool reciting the Gettysburg Address.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: So we finally went on to this college to play this -- play this concert or dance. I think It was a dance. And there was a lot of Northern kids at this college from New York and everything. So the thing went over good. So they invited us to the frat house after we got through.

So finally Max said, 'You want to go?' 'Yeah, we'll go.' So after the job was through we went to this fraternity house, and these kids were having a ball. And so it was -- it was -- I've been (inaudible), and we're down here, and these girls and things were pulling on us and everything. I said, Max, I said, look. Let's get out of here, because first thing you know, if the cops come up here and catch us in here, we're all going to get a beating, you know.

Max says, 'okay, let's go.' So we left them. And just as we pulled out, the state troopers pulled in. Now, we're hungry. We're looking for a place to eat. Every place we stop, we couldn't get no place to eat. We're down below Washington. So just out of Washington coming up we find a Howard Johnson's, and so Max says, 'Let's go in here and eat. You know, we'll get something to see if the man will feed us.'

So Max gets out, goes into the cafe, and he asked, find out if they'll feed us. So the man said, 'well, we'll set you over in the back and the side, see. So he comes out, tells us that we could all go in to sit down and wait there until some of the customers start to get up and leave and everything.
And so the man finally decides that he wouldn't serve us.
Because he was losing all his --

Max jumps up on the stool and says, "Four score and seven years ago our ..." He started reciting the Lincoln Gettysburg Address, you know. And so I said, Max, you better come on. And the cook, the black cook in the kitchen was frantic. He didn't know what the -- he was back there looking, and he was afraid, see, because he said -- Probably these guys are going to get us all lynched down here.
And finally I pulled Max off the stool and we got back in the car and pulled off on away from there.
Yes, every time I see him, I start to --
